area: IDE server lifecycle for the Code view
properties: Only Stop ends a server; every server that may run, a lost start included, is listed, counted and stoppable and survives a World restart; at most one server per folder per host; a route reaches only its issued instance and generation, a retired route never reaches a server again and nothing is retargeted; a removed SSH host shows as unreachable with a by-hand stop and Forget
assessment: Bounded model of two folders (local and SSH) under a one-server limit, with lost answers, ghost scripts, World restart, reconnects, connection removal, disable, forward drops, crashes and re-parented terminals, checked exhaustively by TLC in a default and a deep (SSH only, two faults) configuration. 300 sampled traces are replayed through the real IdeService and IdeInstances against a fake host; eight model flags each give a counterexample. Two counterexamples found in the first design (an Open queued past a connection removal, a look that forgot an unanswered start) were fixed and are kept as witnesses that the fixed service rejects and the service with each fix taken out follows.
remaining: Independent review. Host scripts are taken from the model in replay and tested separately with real sh; the server stopping on its own after a timeout, timeouts and downloads are not modelled; one browser origin is covered by route tests, not the model.
